tool_input.description: Check Java String.lastIndexOf behavior with empty search and negative start

result:
All 62 tests pass against the actual implementation. I wrote a self-contained JUnit 5 test class covering `Strings` (both `CS`/`CI` singletons and a `Builder`-constructed instance): `compare`, `contains`/`containsAny`, `endsWith`/`endsWithAny`, both `equals` overloads (including the non-`String` `CharSequence` branch) and `equalsAny`, both `indexOf`/`lastIndexOf` overloads with boundary/negative start positions, `appendIfMissing`/`prependIfMissing` with extra varargs, `remove`/`removeStart`/`removeEnd`, `replace`/`replaceOnce` (including a long-running replace to stress the internal capacity estimate), `startsWith`/`startsWithAny`, and the package-private `initialCapacity` helper (including overflow clamping to `ArrayUtils.SAFE_MAX_ARRAY_LENGTH`).

I didn't find any discrepancies between the documented behavior and the actual code — every assertion I wrote against the javadoc-specified contract passed, so no bugs are reported.

One thing worth flagging for awareness (not asserted as a bug, since it's explicitly documented): `Strings.CI.indexOf("abc", "", 9)` returns `-1` even though the abstract method's general contract states "a start position greater than the string length only matches an empty search CharSequence" (which would suggest `3`, matching `CS`'s behavior for the same input). Since the `CI`-specific javadoc example explicitly asserts `-1` as the intended result, I treated it as documented, intentional asymmetry rather than a bug — but you may want to double check that intent.

Test file: `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/StringsAgentTest.java`.
